title: Trace the search-serving path under pressure
description: Choose a scenario to see which dependencies are on the request path, what degrades, and which hard filters still protect the final result set. Select a component to inspect its responsibility.

nodes.label: Searcher
nodes.detail: Sends a query, locale, safe session context, and request deadline. The client never decides eligibility.

nodes.label: Query gateway
nodes.detail: Normalizes the query, resolves requester policy and experiment assignment, and carries the deadline through every synchronous call.

nodes.label: Result cache
nodes.detail: Serves a cacheable result only when its query, cohort, policy, and index keys match. Time-sensitive eligibility still runs before display.

nodes.label: Hybrid retrieval
nodes.detail: Runs lexical and vector retrieval over the authorized corpus and returns a broad candidate set with document versions.

nodes.label: Ranking service
nodes.detail: Uses a cheap first stage for many candidates and a richer reranker for a bounded top set. It obeys the remaining request budget.

nodes.label: Eligibility gate
nodes.detail: Applies access, legal, moderation, availability, deduplication, and diversity rules before the result page is released.

nodes.label: Online features
nodes.detail: Serves bounded query, session, and document features with schema and freshness metadata. It is not the authority for access or inventory.

nodes.label: Interaction stream
nodes.detail: Records impressions, positions, clicks, and satisfaction outcomes outside the response path for evaluation and training.

nodes.label: Training pipeline
nodes.detail: Builds debiased, versioned examples and evaluates candidate models before they can reach serving.

scenarios.label: Cache hit
scenarios.summary: A version-matched cached result can skip retrieval and scoring, but it still reaches the eligibility gate before display and emits an impression asynchronously.
scenarios.result: The shortest path preserves correctness: cache speed does not grant permission to serve a stale or unauthorized result.

scenarios.label: Normal cache miss
scenarios.summary: The service retrieves broad candidates, joins fresh features for the bounded rerank, applies final eligibility, and logs the displayed positions outside the deadline.
scenarios.result: A multi-stage pipeline spends expensive compute only after retrieval has narrowed the corpus and hard constraints remain in force.

scenarios.label: Feature outage
scenarios.summary: Online personalization features are unavailable. The ranking service uses a preapproved non-personalized feature subset and preserves final policy checks.
scenarios.result: Relevance may fall, but the service remains available with an observable fallback. It does not invent personal features or bypass eligibility.

scenarios.label: Reranker pressure
scenarios.summary: Tail latency or saturation makes the rich reranker unsafe to call. The service returns first-stage ordering after policy and diversity checks.
scenarios.result: Skipping optional work protects the deadline. The fallback is deliberately less precise, not less safe.

scenarios.label: Eligibility failure
scenarios.summary: The policy dependency cannot confirm access or required product constraints for this surface, so the affected result set must not be released.
scenarios.result: Fail closed or omit the affected results. A response that is fast but violates an eligibility constraint is not a valid fallback.
